ai.title: Disable custom Fireworks deployments in web LLM API
ai.summary: The `FIREWORKS_USE_CUSTOM_DEPLOYMENT` flag in `web/src/llm-api/fireworks.ts` is set to `false`. This forces the application to use the global Fireworks API exclusively, bypassing the `FIREWORKS_DEPLOYMENT_MAP` configuration. The change is scoped to the web client's LLM API integration. Custom deployment IDs remain defined in the map but are currently unused.

eli5.text: Starting today, the web-based assistant always connects to the shared Fireworks service instead of trying to reach any dedicated, custom deployments. If you use the web client, you won't notice anything change in day-to-day use, but behind the scenes the option to route requests to a separate deployment has been turned off, so all model requests now go through the standard global endpoint. Custom deployment IDs are still listed in the configuration but are no longer consulted, meaning they have no effect right now.

ai.title: Add query-usage-stats.ts script for LLM token metrics
ai.summary: New internal script scripts/query-usage-stats.ts queries the message table for token usage stats. Calculates average input/output tokens, cache hit rate, requests per second (median/peak), and client request volume for specific models like minimax-m2.5. Used for internal capacity planning and model performance monitoring.

eli5.text: The team added a behind-the-scenes tool that quietly scans how much the assistant is being used each day. It quietly watches usage numbers like how many times people ask the assistant to do something, how many of those questions get answered using saved shortcuts instead of starting from scratch, and how busy the service gets at its busiest hour. Only the team running the service can use it today. You wouldn't see it change anything you do, but it helps them decide if they need to add more computers to keep everything fast.
